subject: forensic-medicine
title: Forensic psychiatry and mental illness in law

steps.tx: Criminal responsibility for mental illness in India has moved from the old penal code to the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita**. The defence applies where, because of **unsoundness of mind**, the accused could not understand what they were doing, or that it was wrong or against the law, at the time of the act. This mirrors the **McNaughten rule**, often called the right or wrong test. Exam questions often ask for the corresponding provision, so learn how the old and new codes map onto each other.

steps.tx: Several tests exist for criminal responsibility. The **Durham rule** holds that an act is not punishable if it resulted from mental disease or defect. The **Currens rule** asks whether the person lacked capacity to regulate conduct according to law because of mental disease. The **irresistible impulse test** focuses on destroyed free agency of the will. India follows McNaughten, so these are compared rather than applied.

Was free agency of the will destroyed?

steps.tx: Perception errors matter in court. A **hallucination** is a false perception without any external stimulus, such as smelling an unpleasant odour when none is present. An **illusion** is a misinterpretation of a real external stimulus. A **delusion** is a false fixed belief not amenable to reason, a disorder of thought content rather than perception. Delusions of infidelity are called **Othello syndrome**.

steps.tx: A **lucid interval** is a period within insanity or epidural haemorrhage when symptoms disappear completely. During it, the person can judge acts soundly, make a valid will, give evidence and is legally liable. Its duration varies and cannot be predicted with certainty. Testamentary capacity is the mental ability to make a valid will, requiring a sound disposing mind at the time of making it.

steps.tx: Impulse disorders and the mentally ill in custody need care. **Kleptomania** is an irresistible desire to steal articles of little value, and **pyromania** an irresistible desire to set fires. **Dipsomania** is periodic craving for alcohol. Under Section 330 CrPC, a magistrate may release an unfit accused on bail or to psychiatric care. **Parasuicide** is a non-fatal self-harm act, with drug overdose the commonest method worldwide.
